title: Convoy TAKA-909, 19 September 1944
eyebrow: South of Honshu and east of Formosa · BANG's third war patrol

paras.text: BANG's attacks on convoy TAKA-909 east of Formosa, as typed on her attack sheets, with her depth log and the 4th Surface Escort Division's record of the day.

No. 2 Tosei Maru sunk. BANG claimed one AK sunk and another probably sunk. CD-30 and Taian Maru, with army aircraft, attacked her and claimed "one enemy submarine sunk"; BANG surfaced that night after about 80 depth charges.

Keelung to Kagoshima, with a section from Naha: ten ships of 34,049 tons under six escorts, in the 4th Surface Escort Division's table of convoys given air cover (jacar:C08030144100 p05). The same diary names the escorts and only the ship sunk; BANG saw 8 merchantmen including an AO, and 5 or more escorts. The escort W-15's diary has the convoy sailing from Keelung for Naha at 0210 I, No. 7 ship Tosei Maru torpedoed at 0820 I at 24-52N 122-23E, five minutes after BANG fired and 8 nm from her, and W-15 leading the convoy back to Keelung; it sailed again the next morning (p. 49, 53) [[cite:jacar:C08030607800]]. The convoy's own record: [[convoy:taka-909]].

Positions are BANG's own dead reckoning and star sights; lines between them are straight, and where she went in between is not recorded. Open circles are ships she sighted, at the target's position. As the clock passes each firing time a red ring pulses at BANG's position; hover a diamond for the attack sheet.
BANG kept zone K (−10) throughout. Japanese records use Tokyo time (I, −9).

Two Japanese records for this patrol give no time: combinedfleet.com's account of convoy No. 3905 and the 4th Surface Escort Division's daily summary for TAKA-909 (W-15's diary gives TAKA-909's, 0820 I). Each is drawn at the time of the attack it matches, and marked so. FRUPAC's intercept has No. 3905's ships "torp & sunk 1520/09" (1520 I = 1620 K, between Attacks 1 and 2).

No Japanese record has been found for Attacks 5 and 6 (20–21 September): the 4th Escort diary has no attack on those days, and W-15's diary has TAKA-909 at sea that night with nothing entered (engagement `bang-east-of-formosa-1944-09-20`). Where the Japanese record names only the ships that were hit, the rest of the convoy is described as BANG saw it.

BANG's third war patrol report, NARA microfilm M1752 (74802831). The 4th Surface Escort Division / Okinawa Base Force war diary, September 1944, and minesweeper W-15's war diary, September 1944, via JACAR (C08030144100, C08030607800, National Institute for Defense Studies). Convoy No. 3905 from combinedfleet.com, a secondary source, flagged where used. Coastline: Natural Earth.

events.title: Ordered 400 ft
events.words: Went immediately to 400 feet as I had seen another escort ... at about 2000 yards with a 0° angle on the bow.

events.title: Ordered 450 ft (80)
events.words: Very deliberate depth charging began 4 minutes after firing. Three escorts ... let us have about 80 charges in patterns of 3 6 or 9 during the next 4½ hours. We were running silent at 450 feet under a 24 degree negative gradient.

events.title: Tosei Maru
events.words: Separate sheet 1. (1) 0820: at E 122°23′ N 24°52′, No. 7 ship Tosei Maru torpedoed. (2) 0830: W-15 leads the convoy back to Keelung. (3) 1256: off Keelung island, leaves the convoy for the scene. (4) 1625: arrives; begins attacking the enemy submarine with CD-30. (5) 1630: receives the report that CD-30, working with aircraft, has certainly sunk the enemy submarine. (6) 1700: breaks off the search for Keelung. (7) 2000: anchors at Keelung

events.note: Minesweeper W-15's war diary, September 1944 (第十五號掃海艇戦時日誌, cover p42; the ship written 東勢丸, without the 第二 of J02 and J04), the 19th's action written up on a separate sheet as the daily page (p49) says. W-15 was one of TAKA-909's six escorts (J06). Its daily page: 0210 sailed escorting TAKA-909 for Naha; 0830 Tosei Maru torpedoed; 2000 anchored at Keelung. Five minutes after BANG's Attacks 3-4 (0915 K = 0815 I), 8 nm east-south-east of her position (24-56N 122-14.5E), and the first record with a time and place for the sinking: J02 has the place but no time, J04's 0925 is 65 minutes later. The convoy put back to Keelung, so the escort's own diary answers the question J06 left open. The 1630 report of a submarine certainly sunk "with aircraft" has the same time and wording (撃沈確實) as the Navy summary's entry for the 953rd Air Group, which the summary puts on the 20th (J05): possibly the same event, dated a day later there. BANG was at 450 ft from 0920 K and came to periscope depth at 1730 K (1630 I) with nothing in sight

paras.text: Attacked by BANG on 19 September 1944 off the north-east coast of Formosa. The Okinawa diary names six escorts and the one ship lost, No. 2 Tosei Maru, and says CD-30 and Taian Maru with army aircraft attacked the submarine and claimed it sunk. BANG surfaced that night after about 80 depth charges.

**Route and size** from the 4th Surface Escort Division's table of convoys given air cover (jacar:C08030144100 p05, read on the image 5 Nov 2026): on the 19th, TAKA-909, ten ships of 34,049 tons, escorted by CD-30, W-15, No. 3 Takunan Maru, Shichiri Maru, Taian Maru and No. 3 Taihei Maru, routed Keelung to Kagoshima and Naha to Kagoshima. So it sailed from Keelung, not Takao as the convoy code had suggested. Its sailing time and cargo are not recorded. The waypoints off Formosa's east coast and Kagoshima Bay are assumed. BANG counted eight merchantmen, one an oiler.

No other US boat's attack on TAKA-909 has been found: the diary's columns for the 18th–21st have only this attack and, on the 20th, an attack on the depot ship Jingei far to the east (N27-12.5 E127-10.0; not BANG's).

**The escort W-15's diary** (jacar:C08030607800, September 1944, read on the images 11 Nov 2026) gives the voyage: sailed from Keelung for Naha at 0210 on the 19th; No. 7 ship Tosei Maru torpedoed at 0820 at 24-52N 122-23E (p53); W-15 led the convoy back to Keelung, anchoring at 2000. The convoy sailed again at 06?0 on the 20th (noon 25-01N 122-21E), anchored at Miyako at 1530 on the 21st (noon 24-51.5N 124-45E), sailed again that evening, and dispersed off Naha at 1350 on the 23rd, W-15 entering at 1520 (p49-p50). No attack is entered for the night of the 20th, when BANG fired at a convoy east of Keelung (engagement `bang-east-of-formosa-1944-09-20`). Times I.
To find: TAKA-909's ships' names and cargo (CD-30's or the other escorts' September diaries, not found on JACAR).

words.type_attack: Day periscope. Had to run under bow and beam escort to get in. Below periscope depth using sound tracking only for 20 minutes prior to firing. Final periscope set-up to TDC just before firing. Fired four torpedoes spread 3, 1, 1, 3 from aft forward using the offset knob on the TDC.
words.description: Convoy consisting of two AK's (best estimate, similar to ADEN MARU, ONI 208J (revised), page 189); one large AO; five unidentified merchantmen; and five or more escorts. Escorts seen only with near 0° angle on the bow, estimated as CHIDORI type. Clear daylight. Fired at ADEN MARU type AK.
words.damaged: One AK (similar to ADEN MARU). EU.
words.determined_by: Heard two timed hits in this AK. Twenty minutes after attack heard slow heavy screws in opposite direction from direction of movement of convoy.
words.target_line: Target Draft: 27 feet Course: 090° Speed: 7.0 Range: 1400 yds.
words.remarks: One miss due to spread, the other probably due to target maneuver during torpedo run or to control errors.
words.note: The damage heading is typed "Ships Damaged or Probably Sunk" (kept as `damaged`).

words.type_attack: Same approach as for Attack No. 3. Immediately after firing bow tubes gave set-up for stern tubes, kept constant bearings to TDC during firing, and applied 3, 1, 1, 3 spread from aft forward by means of the offset knob on the TDC.
words.description: Same convoy as Attack No. 3. Fired at ADEN MARU type AK.
words.sunk: One AK (similar to ADEN MARU). EU.
words.determined_by: Heard two timed hits in this AK. Heard prolonged breaking up noises through hull.
words.target_line: Target Draft: 27 feet Course: 090° Speed: 7.0 Range: 1200 yds.
words.remarks: One miss due to spread, the other probably due to target maneuver during torpedo run or to control errors.
words.note: The sheet's time is typed "0915-55(K)": 55 seconds after 0915, the stern tubes fired "immediately after firing bow tubes" (type attack). positions.csv has the minute, 0915 (it had 0955 until 31 Oct 2026, the seconds read as minutes); attacks.csv keeps 0915-55. The typed tracks (76P to 85P) run about 9° short of what own course 340 + gyro (205 to 196) against target course 090 gives (85P to 94P); they would fit an own course near 349. The sheet types one own-ship line, the same as Attack 3's, for both salvos; the boat may have swung while the stern set-up was made. Kept as typed (re-read at zoom: 205/202/199/196, 76P/79P/82P/85P; own course 340° on p19).
